summary: This work develops a complete fault-tolerant logical instruction set for a family of lifted-product (LP) quantum error-correcting codes by identifying a canonical logical basis with cyclic and row-column-parallel structure. The canonical LP codes achieve high rates with distances up to 20, encoding hundreds to thousands of logical qubits while supporting low-overhead modular gate implementations and highly parallel measurements.
motivation: High-rate qLDPC codes promise dramatic reductions in physical-qubit overhead for quantum computation, but realizing efficient fault-tolerant logic on high-density encodings remains challenging because generic code-agnostic techniques incur substantial overhead when applied to arbitrary codes without exploiting code structure.
method: We co-design the code structure with its logical instruction set by characterizing when LP codes over cyclic groups admit a canonical logical basis inherited from classical codewords. This structure enables constant-depth automorphism and fold-transversal Clifford gates, modular graph-surgery gadgets requiring only $r_A$ seed surgery gadgets (independent of lift size $l$), compact canonical extractors smaller than half the code block, and parallel intra- and inter-column measurements via hypergraph surgery with proven distance preservation.
result: For $[[1122,148,\leq 20]]$ and $[[4350,1224,\leq 20]]$ canonical LP codes, we construct explicit fault-tolerant gadgets: only 2 and 4 seed surgery gadgets respectively, extractors requiring $<50\%$ overhead, parallel magic-state injection from surface codes into full code blocks with phenomenological distance $\geq\min(d,d_s)$, and verified soundness $\rho_d\geq 1$ for all seed gadgets.
